1	import { z } from 'zod';
     2	
     3	/**
     4	 * Insight scope enum.
     5	 * - 'global'  — applies across all projects
     6	 * - 'project' — scoped to a specific project
     7	 *
     8	 * Note: when scope === 'project', project_slug must be present. This constraint
     9	 * is enforced by the storage layer rather than this schema, so the Zod schema
    10	 * remains composable and usable without runtime context.
    11	 */
    12	export const InsightScope = z.enum(['global', 'project']);
    13	export type InsightScope = z.infer<typeof InsightScope>;
    14	
    15	/**
    16	 * Regex pattern for valid project slugs.
    17	 *
    18	 * Accepts slugs that start with an alphanumeric character and contain only
    19	 * letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens. Rejects anything with `/`, `\`,
    20	 * `.`, spaces, or other characters that could escape the `.knowledge/` directory.
    21	 *
    22	 * This pattern is the single source of truth — used by both the Zod schema
    23	 * (InsightSchema.project_slug) and the storage-layer guard (_validateSlug).
    24	 * Update this constant to change the slug policy in both places at once.
    25	 */
    26	export const PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX = /^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$/;
    27	
    28	/**
    29	 * Insight schema — a single reusable knowledge record stored in the knowledge base.
    30	 *
    31	 * Field notes:
    32	 * - `project_slug`: required when scope === 'project', but that constraint is
    33	 *   owned by the storage layer (KnowledgeStoreManager), not this schema. The
    34	 *   schema accepts project_slug as optional to remain context-free. The regex
    35	 *   constraint (PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX: `^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$`) prevents
    36	 *   path traversal at the schema boundary — slugs with `/`, `\`, or `..` are
    37	 *   rejected.
    38	 * - `confidence`: a 0–1 float indicating reliability of the insight. Range is
    39	 *   enforced as [0, 1] — values outside this range are rejected at parse time.
    40	 * - `superseded_by`: optional reference to the id of the insight that replaces
    41	 *   this one. No referential integrity is enforced at the schema layer.
    42	 * - `updated_at`: optional; present only when an insight has been amended after
    43	 *   initial creation.
    44	 */
    45	export const InsightSchema = z.object({
    46	  id: z.number().int(),
    47	  scope: InsightScope,
    48	  project_slug: z.string().regex(PROJECT_SLUG_REGEX).optional(),
    49	  title: z.string(),
    50	  content: z.string(),
    51	  category: z.string(),
    52	  tags: z.array(z.string()),
    53	  source: z.string(),
    54	  created_at: z.string(),
    55	  updated_at: z.string().optional(),
    56	  confidence: z.number().min(0).max(1),
    57	  superseded_by: z.number().int().optional(),
    58	});
    59	export type Insight = z.infer<typeof InsightSchema>;
    60	
    61	/**
    62	 * KnowledgeStore schema — top-level structure for `.knowledge/store.json`.
    63	 *
    64	 * - `version`: schema version string (e.g. "1.0.0") for forward-compatibility.
    65	 * - `last_updated`: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent write.
    66	 * - `next_id`: auto-increment counter; the id that will be assigned to the
    67	 *   next insight added to the store.
    68	 * - `insights`: flat array of all stored Insight records.
    69	 */
    70	export const KnowledgeStoreSchema = z.object({
    71	  version: z.string(),
    72	  last_updated: z.string(),
    73	  next_id: z.number().int().nonnegative(),
    74	  insights: z.array(InsightSchema),
    75	});
    76	export type KnowledgeStore = z.infer<typeof KnowledgeStoreSchema>;
